failures_and_limits: Initial preparation accessed a pikepdf MediaBox after its temporary owner was destroyed. It failed before Wine; retained artifacts were not used. The corrected preparation retains the page box while its owner is open.
Initial analysis assumed every candidate contained each glyph; d1 nested text produced no ink. The corrected analyzer records missing glyphs instead of treating blank pages as successful rendering.
The high-900 split d1 capture has different detected frame dimensions. Strict comparison is rejected and retained; it is not aligned, resized or replaced.

The four-session normalization host runner exited143 during setup. Docker inspection confirmed every original container live. Numeric controls were read, those same sessions resumed at75%, and captures/cleanup completed without restarts. The cause of the host signal is unknown.
Nested d1 text remains absent after coordinate normalization. Both rectangle path controls paint identical visible pixels. This concerns the tested viewer path, not universal Type3 support.

Original glyph paths paint in all28frames but every complete frame regresses. Two point-coordinate glyphs are absent on reversed100%controls (42x42 Chinese Wen in direct,28x28 A in split); normalized axis controls restore them. No exact tight glyph bitmap is found among760comparisons, including these2missingglyphs; this is not an adopted output mode.

Original font programs, source-order semantic text and mathematical geometry are retained in the nested-text controls. Path controls deliberately change the drawing primitive using the same glyph IDs/outlines; selected glyphs have no per-glyph instructions. Rectangle controls deliberately replace glyph shapes.

Two independent cold source repeats match exactly; no fresh actual-corpus compatibility or runtime parity claim is made. The77actual pages remain at the previous implementation state, all with pixel differences.
No vendor implementation, foreign converter or private HN/JBIG source was inspected. Font outlines are external data; no font/PDF/document/screenshot binary is published.
